findings.text: non-blocking: _process_environment is a byte-for-byte duplicate of reckon/crew/process_signal.py:127 (same name, same /proc/<pid>/environ split), and _parent_process at :676 restates the ancestor-walk capability already owned by reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:369 _parent_of and _ancestor_pids; the addition neither extends nor wraps either owner, so the fence's recovery logic forks two low-level readers the repository already maintains.

non-blocking: the done_when requires that the tests importing the scheduler shim add no failure against the base, but both recorded arms (manifest.md:25-26) run only tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py, neither of which imports reckon/nested_launch.py or the shims, so the 58-to-64 pair cannot see a regression in the changed module; the direct importer tests/test_nested_launch.py is in no arm, and the manifest's rubric.done_when claim that the scoped gate ran them green is unsupported because the scoped gate lists the same two unrelated files.

non-blocking: ancestry_fence's own termination - ANCESTRY_BOUND, the parent<=0/seen cycle guard and the namespace-init stop - has no test; test_f at :314 injects a lambda and pins only fence_environment's fill-only-missing rule, so a regression in the walk's stopping condition (for example an off-by-one that skipped the nearest ancestor) would leave all six cases green.

non-blocking: the recovery depends on a live ancestor still holding RECKON_WORKER_FENCE in its exec-time environment, but the fence sets the recipe with --setenv on the bwrap payload only (reckon/_worker_fence.py:2449), so a worker that clears its environment and then exec-replaces itself leaves only bwrap above it, whose /proc environ carries no recipe; fence_environment then returns {} and the submission is passed through bare rather than refused, which is the outcome the goal sentence forbids.
